slides.sub: 3 steps to check any NJ address, and why it can change your monthly cost.

slides.label: High-risk flood area
slides.body: A home in a high-risk flood area has at least a 1 in 4 chance of flooding during a 30-year mortgage.
slides.source: FEMA, Flood Maps and Zones Explained (Oct. 2026)

slides.title: Look up the address
slides.body: Type the address into FEMA's Flood Map Service Center at msc.fema.gov. Zones that start with A or V are high-risk areas.
slides.source: FEMA Flood Map Service Center; FEMA, Flood Maps and Zones Explained (Oct. 2026)

slides.title: Read the seller's flood disclosure
slides.body: NJ sellers have to tell you if the home's in a FEMA flood area and about flood damage they know of. Talk to a real estate attorney about your situation.
slides.source: NJ DCA, Flood risk disclosure tools announcement (Oct. 2026)

slides.title: Get a flood insurance quote early
slides.body: Most homeowners policies don't cover floods. If the home's in a high-risk area and your lender is federally regulated or insured, flood insurance is required. Talk to a licensed lender for your numbers.
slides.source: FEMA FloodSmart; FEMA, Flood Maps and Zones Explained (Oct. 2026)
